q: The buildings look too pixelated. How many pixels per cell should the world art use?
ctx: I checked all 26 buildings on one sheet (picture 4). They pass every technical rule (palette, clean edges, sizes). 8 are drawn from the corner instead of the front, and 10 more need a clean-up (single-pixel noise, too narrow for their footprint, weak outline); those 18 get fixed whatever you pick. Two things make them look blocky. (1) Today's zoom draws each art pixel 1, 2 or 3 screen pixels wide (picture 1); the crisp zoom steps you already picked fix that. (2) The art has 32 pixels per cell, so at the closest zoom each art pixel is a 3-4 px block. 64 pixels per cell keeps every building the same size on screen with 4 times the pixels (picture 2, made from the artist's own drawing of the Spring). Mixing 64 and 32 shows when you zoom in close (picture 3). Cost: each piece in the chosen scope is redrawn once (about the same work per piece as a clean redraw, because the artist draws at high resolution anyway); the 19 new buildings would be drawn at the new density from the start. With 64 px art, the 20-cell zoom step shows slightly uneven fine pixels and the far 60-cell step can flicker a little when panning; the 15- and 30-cell steps stay crisp. My pick: 64 for everything standing on the ground, because that is where the eye goes; the calmer ground you picked hides the mix, and the coasts you signed off stay as they are.

One object, same size on screen: 16 / 32 (today) / 64 px per cell / painted
Closest zoom: a 64 px object next to 32 px grass and bush

o: Keep 32 px per cell: clean redraw of the 18 weak buildings only (front view, less noise). Crisp after the zoom fix, but still chunky up close
64 px per cell for buildings only (the 26 existing and the 19 new ones); nodes, trees, props and ground stay 32

64 px per cell for everything standing on the ground: buildings, resource nodes, trees, props, NPCs and creatures; ground and coast tiles stay 32. Start with a 3-building pilot (Paper Mill, Kiln, Workbench) that you check in game first
64 px per cell for all world art: everything above, plus ground, coast walls, items and icons (the maximal option; it also redoes the coasts you signed off)
Leave pixel art: a hi-res painted look (smooth, no visible pixels) for all world art
Decide after you see the crisp zoom steps in game; until then only the 8 corner-view buildings are redrawn, at 32

q: Pixelify Sans makes 5 look like S, 1 like 7, 3 and B like 8, E like C and ( ) like { }. Which font should the game use for text and numbers?
ctx: Picture 1 is the game today at 1920x1080: the quest panel shows 0/450 as '0/4S0' and Iron Bar 0/10 as '0/70', a build cost of 25 reads '2S', and in Help '[B] opens the build menu' reads '(8) opens...'. I already show key names as key-caps ([B], [Q] / [E], [Esc]) and fixed the layout bugs from the UI check, but the look-alikes are in Pixelify's letter shapes themselves: picture 2, row B shows that 33 px (3 screen pixels per font pixel) is bigger but still reads 5 as S and B as 8. Picture 2 compares the candidates with the same lines at their crisp sizes, drawn from the real font files with hard pixel edges like the game. Jersey 10 at 30 px (3 screen pixels per font pixel) keeps the pixel look, tells every pair apart and takes the same line width as Pixelify at 22 px, so the panels keep their size (it is only a little taller). VT323 is very clear but thin and typewriter-like. Atkinson Hyperlegible is a smooth font made for legibility, not pixel art. Picture 3 shows the others I tried and why they fall short (Micro 5, Press Start 2P, Silkscreen, Tiny5, DotGothic16); m5x7 / m6x11 were left out because their licence is not clearly OFL or CC0. Every candidate shown is SIL Open Font License (free to ship; the licence file goes into the repo with the font). On phones all text uses the smooth (SDF) cut at 3-4 screen pixels per font pixel, so the choice looks the same there, just larger. My pick: keep Pixelify Sans for titles and headings (the look you chose stays) and use Jersey 10 for body text and every number, as one fixed rule across all panels, pills and tooltips.

imgs.cap: In game now (1920x1080): Help key names, quest numbers, build costs and world pills in Pixelify Sans 22 px
Same lines, real font files at crisp sizes: A Pixelify 22 (now), B Pixelify 33, C Jersey 10, D VT323, E Atkinson Hyperlegible
Also tried and not offered: Micro 5, Press Start 2P, Silkscreen, Tiny5, DotGothic16

o: Keep Pixelify Sans at 22 px everywhere as it is (key-caps [B] stay; 5 / S and B / 8 stay alike)
Pixelify Sans at 33 px for body text (bigger and crisper, but 5 / S and B / 8 still look alike, and every panel grows by half)
Keep Pixelify for all letters; draw only digits and number signs (0-9 / + - : x %) in Jersey 10. Fixes every number; key letters like B and E stay as they are
Pixelify Sans for titles and headings; Jersey 10 for body text and all numbers (same line width as today)
Pixelify Sans for titles and headings; VT323 for body text and all numbers
Replace Pixelify everywhere with Jersey 10 (titles too: one pixel font for all text)
Pixelify Sans for titles; a smooth, non-pixel font (Atkinson Hyperlegible) for body text and numbers
All of them as a player choice in Menu > Settings ("Text font": Pixelify only, Pixelify titles + Jersey 10, Jersey 10 only, VT323, Smooth); the game starts on Pixelify titles + Jersey 10
